scenario: A buyer wants one over-ear headphone for home desk use through 2036. The total budget is $80, open-back leakage is acceptable, and the available source can drive 250-ohm headphones. Serviceability and continued passive operation come before wireless convenience or ANC.

rules.product_serviceability_matrix_v1: Compare the frozen price, wired or wireless path, headband and cable construction, explicitly declared replacement scope, battery dependence, impedance, and open- or closed-back tradeoff for all three candidates. Absence of a replacement claim is not proof that repair is impossible.
rules.battery_degradation_scope_v1: Treat rechargeable-battery capacity fade as a physical aging mechanism whose rate depends on cycling, temperature, state of charge, and other conditions. Do not convert the general mechanism into a guaranteed failure date for a particular headphone.
rules.owner_evidence_scope_v1: Use long-use and repair anecdotes to identify possible failure and maintenance paths, while keeping model identity explicit. Other-model accounts cannot prove a candidate will last a decade.
rules.ten_year_serviceability_decision_v1: Under the stated home-use, impedance, leakage, budget, and serviceability priorities, select the DT 990 PRO because its frozen listing explicitly describes a wired spring-steel design whose parts are replaceable. Preserve the caveats that this is seller evidence, its cable is a long coiled single-sided design, and the frozen community pages are not same-model decade validation.
